 Concerns about public judgment followed Drew Barrymore into motherhood, as the actress revealed how her previous party lifestyle affected her confidence in raising her children. During a November 17 episode of The Drew Barrymore Show, she discussed the shame she experienced and the criticism she feared after becoming a parent.
 Barrymore shares two daughters, Olive, 14, and Frankie, 12, with her ex-husband, Will Kopelman. She explained that her past experiences and public reputation made her question how others would view her ability to raise children.
 Advertisement 
 Scroll To Continue with Content 
 Speaking with guest Jordan Firstman, Barrymore described the stigma surrounding people who enjoy nightlife and social activities.

 Brittany Snow Announces Engagement to Hunter Moreno 
 “One of the many things I wanted to discuss with you was how much of my life I have spent in shame because of being a party culture person. And I don’t know why, but there’s a villainization of people who want to let loose, who want to imbibe, who want to dance, who want to let go and just get away from this very, very complex world sometimes,” Barrymore told Firstman.
 She also recalled facing repeated questions from journalists about whether she intended to have children. Those questions intensified her concerns about how her public history might affect her future family.
 “And I know what they were saying is, ‘You are not capable, and if you even dared to have children, will they be able to live with the history that is so public?’” she explained.
 Also Read 
 Florence Pugh Rejects Cosmetic Surgery Rumors After Awards Appearance 
 Barrymore said the criticism became particularly difficult after she became a mother. She rejected the assumption that people associated with party culture are necessarily bad parents.
 “And when I became a parent, that haunted me so badly, the judgment and ‘the partiers are bad people,’ and I don’t think that’s true,” she said.
 The actress has also spoken openly about the challenges of learning how to raise children. During a 2022 appearance on Chicks in the Office, she acknowledged that she did not initially have the routines and parenting knowledge she associated with other families.
 Also Read 
 Jon Hamm and Anna Osceola Welcome First Child 
 “All those parents who have it all together, and they’ve got hygiene and nutrition and schedules and boundaries, God bless you,” Barrymore said.
 She acknowledged that becoming a parent required learning many responsibilities without having a clear guide. Her early experiences sometimes left her feeling overwhelmed and uncertain about her abilities.
 “I didn’t know any of that stuff when I had my kids,” she said.
 Also Read 
 Lysandre Nadeau Recalls Son Blaise's Christmas Health Crisis 
 Barrymore also described the emotional difficulties of adjusting to motherhood and the pressure she placed on herself during that period.
 “I did not have the blueprint and I felt like a failure a lot,” she admitted. “I felt really overwhelmed and like, ‘I don’t know what I’m doing.’”
 Despite those early struggles, Barrymore has previously described raising her children as a defining part of her personal development. In a 2015 interview with E! News, she expressed how much her family meant to her.
 Also Read

 “I just love having a family,” she told E! News in 2015. “I love my kids—I feel so blessed. I feel like I've never been better as a person [than I am] through my family.”
 She also reflected on how becoming a parent changed her perspective on life and her priorities.
 “I feel like I was born the day my kids were,” she added, “and everything in life was like an experiment to learn to apply to them.”
